library(tidyverse)

## Introduction

<!-- Where do the data come from? Who collected them, when and how? -->

The data describe 40 batches from a pilot-plant reactor: the shift that ran each batch, the
catalyst used, the operating conditions, and the yield and purity of the product. They are
fictional, made for this course, but they behave like real process data.

## The data

```{r}
#| label: data
batches <- read_csv("data/reactor_batches.csv")   # replace with your own file
glimpse(batches)
```

<!-- Describe each variable you'll use: what it measures, its units, and its type
     (numerical continuous/discrete, categorical nominal/ordinal). A small table works well. -->

| Variable | Meaning | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `catalyst` | Which of four catalysts was used (A to D) | Categorical (nominal) |
| `residence_min` | Residence time in the reactor, in minutes | Numerical (continuous) |
| `alarms` | Number of process alarms during the batch | Numerical (discrete) |
| `yield_pct` | Yield, as a percentage of the theoretical maximum | Numerical (continuous) |
| ... | ... | ... |

## Exploring the data

### Question 1

```{r}
#| label: q1-summary
batches |>
  group_by(catalyst) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_yield = mean(yield_pct),
    sd_yield = sd(yield_pct),
    median_yield = median(yield_pct)
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: q1-plot
#| fig-cap: "Yield by catalyst."
ggplot(batches, aes(x = catalyst, y = yield_pct)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(x = "Catalyst", y = "Yield (%)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Inference

### A confidence interval

```{r}
#| label: ci
t.test(batches$yield_pct)$conf.int
```

<!-- Interpret it in a full sentence, in context. -->

### A hypothesis test

<!-- State H0 and HA, check the assumptions, run the test, and report the conclusion
     together with the size of the effect. -->

```{r}
#| label: test
a_vs_d <- filter(batches, catalyst %in% c("A", "D"))
t.test(yield_pct ~ catalyst, data = a_vs_d)
```
